newsitem.title: CHINA: China central banker sees loan improvement - paper.
newsitem.headline: China central banker sees loan improvement - paper.

text.p: China's banking system will be able to reduce non-performing loans to 10 percent of total lending from the current 20 percent in seven or eight years, a senior central bank official was quoted on Friday as saying.

Chen Yuan, vice governor of the People's Bank of China, said the improvement would reflect a request by authorities that the nation's state banks reduce their non-performing loans by two to three percent a year and increase the quality of new loans.

Chinese banks were also strengthening their risk control systems, improving criteria for making loans, and holding branch managers responsible for non-performing loans and preventing fraud, the official said in an interview with the Asian Wall Street Journal.
Chen's figure for non-performing loans compared to total loans was considerably higher than previous central bank estimates of 13-14 percent.
It matched the low end of a recent estimate of the U.S. economic forecasting firm DRI/McGraw Hill which said 20-40 percent of all outstanding loans in China's banking system were non-performing.
That study, dismissed by central bank officials, concluded that China's non-performing loans were one of the most serious threats to global market stability.
